messages.content: Please refresh the June 10-17 Kauai comparison before I decide. I need airfare for two, each resort's full seven-night cost, and the car, with the cancellation terms checked again.

The nonstop flights are now $1,418.40 total for two travelers, up $42.40 since the last check. The same pay-later midsize rental from June 10 through June 17 remains $548.20. Koloa Bay's oceanfront king is $4,447.97 for seven nights including taxes and mandatory charges, bringing that trip to $6,414.57. Hanalei Shore's complete seven-night hotel estimate is $4,901.96, bringing its trip to $6,868.56.
Hanalei is still advertising the lower nightly rate. Break down why its total is higher.

Hanalei's room charge is lower, but the seven-night figure adds $385 in resort fees, $280 for parking, and an estimated $238 for breakfast for two. Those items are included in the $4,901.96 comparison. Koloa Bay includes breakfast and parking in its package, so its higher room rate produces the lower complete total.
And the oceanfront room at Koloa is actually still available, not just showing in an old result?

I rechecked live inventory. One refundable oceanfront king remains for all seven nights at Koloa Bay. The resort is labeling it as the last room in that category. Hanalei still has several deluxe ocean-view kings available.
Confirm the exact deadlines and what becomes nonrefundable. Also tell me whether either airfare quote can be refunded to the card.

Koloa Bay requires a two-night deposit of $1,270.85. It is refundable if canceled by 6:00 p.m. Hawaii time on June 3; after that, the deposit is forfeited. Hanalei Shore can be canceled without penalty through 4:00 p.m. Hawaii time on June 5, after which one night's room and tax, $571.84, is charged. The car can be canceled without charge before pickup. The airfare is changeable for airline credit under the fare rules, but it is not refundable to the original payment method.
Run through the actual travel times once more. I want the hotel arrival and departure implications, not only the flight numbers.

The outbound nonstop leaves SFO at 9:10 a.m. June 10 and reaches LIH at 11:52 a.m. After collecting the car, estimated arrival is about 1:20 p.m. at Koloa Bay or 1:45 p.m. at Hanalei Shore. Both properties will hold luggage before their 4:00 p.m. check-in. On June 17, the return leaves LIH at 1:05 p.m. and arrives at SFO at 9:18 p.m. Allowing for fuel and the rental return, departure should be about 9:35 a.m. from Koloa or 9:10 a.m. from Hanalei.
So the flights and car are identical, Koloa saves $453.99 overall, and choosing it also avoids separate breakfast and parking charges. Is that correct?
Correct. The difference between the refreshed totals is $453.99. Koloa Bay is $6,414.57 complete versus $6,868.56 at Hanalei Shore, using the same $1,418.40 airfare and $548.20 rental in both plans.
Book June 10-17 at Koloa Bay in that refundable oceanfront king, and book the nonstop flights and pay-later car from the comparison. Do not book Hanalei.
Before I place all three reservations, please confirm that you accept the airfare being nonrefundable to the card and the Koloa deposit becoming nonrefundable after 6:00 p.m. Hawaii time June 3.
Confirmed. Proceed with Koloa, the nonstop flights, and the car.

The June 10-17, 2028 Kauai trip is booked. The nonstop flights for two are confirmed under H7K2QM at $1,418.40. Koloa Bay Resort's oceanfront king is confirmed under KB8F41 at $4,447.97, with a $1,270.85 deposit charged and refundable through 6:00 p.m. Hawaii time June 3. The pay-later midsize rental is reserved under LIH6R28 at an estimated $548.20 and remains cancelable before pickup. The complete projected trip total is $6,414.57. No reservation was made at Hanalei Shore.
